Hi Jennifer — thanks again for today’s call, really helpful context. Short recap and a couple of asks so we can prepare the DPA/annex your legal team will want to see.

Recap (from our call):
- Redwood will be providing hosted inference for your patient anonymization pipeline (real-time calls from a staging environment).
- Data types: primarily low-risk PII (first/last names, hashed MRNs in staging), occasional PHI in production for de-identification tests — you flagged strict residency and retention rules.
- Residency: production data must stay in us-west region (no cross-border replication).
- Retention: tiered retention — staging logs 7 days, production model inputs 30 days, audit logs 90 days.

Asks / open items for your legal/security:
1) Controller vs Processor: can you confirm Acme wants Redwood to act solely as Processor for all inference traffic (including staging)? If there are parts where you expect RMB (redwood) to be controller please flag.
2) Subprocessors: we have an approved subprocessors list (storage, monitoring). Can you share any vendors you must block?
3) Breach notification: Acme’s RTO/RPO or required notification SLA? We typically accept 72 hours for incident notification to customers but can escalate for enterprise.
4) Documents: attaching a quick data map and our standard DPA for your legal to review.

Next steps proposed:
- You to confirm controller/processor stance and any blocked subprocessors (reply).
- If you want Redline, send it to acme.legal@acmehealth.com and cc me; I’ll route to our legal/infosec.
- We’ll provision a scoped test instance in us-west and share networking info once legal confirms.

Attachments: SaaS_Data_Map.xlsx (data flows), Redwood_Standard_DPA.pdf (link below).

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call with your lawyers if helpful.

Best,

Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary, super helpful. Quick answers and a few clarifying questions from legal — copied our counsel.

1) Controller/Processor: Acme intends for Redwood to be a Processor for the production inference flow. For staging, we need Redwood to handle data as if it were production (same obligations) — treat both the same in the DPA.

2) Subprocessors: we can’t approve any subprocessors that perform long-term persistence of raw inputs outside our region. Please provide a list of current and proposed subprocessors and indicate which ones have access to blob storage or audit logs.

3) Breach notice: Acme requires initial notification within 24 hours of detection for incidents impacting PHI. Follow-up with root-cause and remediation plan within 72 hours. Is Redwood able to commit to 24-hour initial notification?

4) Data residency & replication: confirm there will be no automatic backups outside us-west and that cross-region read-replicas are disabled for this account.

Attached is a first-pass redline of your DPA from our legal (Acme_DPA_Redline_v1.pdf). Our counsel would prefer to run the updated DPA by you and then set a short legal sync to finalize.

One more operational note: do you retain request/response pairs for training/quality by default? If so, we need explicit opt-out and a guarantee that any retention for QA is anonymized.

Happy to jump on a call with your legal and infosec next week.

Thanks,
Jennifer Huang

Hi Jennifer, Marissa, Ben — looping in answers from legal and engineering below.

Controller/Processor
- Accepted: Redwood will be Processor for both staging and production for the scope described. We'll reflect that language in the DPA (Article 1.1 and definitions).

Subprocessors
- Attached is our current subprocessors list and a short matrix indicating which subprocessors have persistent access to object storage or logs. We can commit to notifying Acme 30 days prior to adding any new subprocessor; we can discuss contractually restricting specific subprocessors if required.

Retention / Training Data
- Default: request/response pairs are retained 30 days for production and 7 days for staging (this aligns with Marissa’s summary).
- Per-tenant opt-out: Engineering can enable a tenant-level flag to disable retention of raw input/outputs and to anonymize any short-term traces used for QA. Ben: we’ll execute a scoped opt-out config for ACME.

Data Residency / Backups
- Confirmed: no automatic cross-region backups for the Acme tenant; we will ensure snapshots and backups are confined to us-west for this account.

Breach Notification SLA
- Standard Redwood policy: initial customer notification within 72 hours of confirmed incident detection.
- Exceptional request: for PHI-impacting incidents we are prepared to commit to 24-hour initial notification, provided: (a) incident is classified and confirmed by Redwood within that window, and (b) Acme provides a primary security contact and an authorized escalation path (email + phone). We will reflect the PHI-specific notification language as an addendum to the DPA.

Next steps
1) Marissa to share our subprocessors list and short matrix to Acme (attached link).
2) Ben to provision the tenant-level retention opt-out and confirm toggles with Jennifer.
3) Rishi to send a redline response to Acme_DPA_Redline_v1.pdf with proposed language for PHI 24-hour notification.
4) Schedule a 30-min legal + infosec sync (Proposed times: Mon/Tue next week).

Jennifer: can you share the primary security contact (name + phone) so we can include it in the contract addendum?
